messages:
anya: Quick POC update — I wired lightweight runtime traces for policy evals (policy decision, score components, matched rules). Want feedback on API shape and perf tradeoffs.

sam: Nice. What are the perf numbers? added latency?

anya: Local microbench: sync eval hook on hotpath +4–7ms median, p95 +12ms when full explain payload is built. Memory ~+8–12MB per worker when trace buffering is enabled.

ravi: Is this going to leak tenant data? we need privacy guardrails before shipping.

anya: Absolutely. Plan is opt-in per-tenant + redaction pipeline. Traces store only rule ids, numeric deltas, and hashed feature keys. Full inputs are redacted by default.

luis: Can we avoid serializing big explain blobs on the request path? Maybe emit a small explain_id upstream and materialize the full trace async to blob store. That keeps tail latency low.

anya: Exactly my thinking. Proposal: sync path returns explain_id and score; async worker persists full trace with explain_id -> TTL'd compressed JSON. Optional direct attach for internal tenants.

maia: How would config look? can we toggle per-deployment?

anya: Sketch config (yaml):
```
policy_eval_instrumentation:
  enabled: true
  sample_rate: 0.01
  inline_explain_threshold_ms: 8   # if building explain exceeds this, return explain_id instead
  persist_endpoint: https://ingest.redwood-observability.svc/put
  redact_keys: ["user_id", "prompt_text"]
```

sam: inline_explain_threshold is smart. But how do adapters/plugins opt into providing structured explain data? we have many policy adapters.

anya: Proposed adapter contract: evaluate(ctx) -> {score: float, explain: optional[structured_explain]}
If explain is present runtime either attaches it (subject to threshold/sample) or persists and returns id. Minimal fallback: adapter returns score + reason_tags.

ravi: Storage cost question — traces per request could be hefty. What's retention plan?

luis: Sample by outcome (errors / degraded LRs) and by canary tenants. Default retention 7d, gzipped + schema versioning. Add size cap per-trace (e.g., 64KB) and drop verbose fields beyond cap.

anya: Agree. Also propose backpressure: if persist queue length > N, drop non-sampled traces and increment metric policy_trace_dropped.

maia: How does this play with Dedicated and Private customers (no external persist endpoint)?

anya: We add two modes: external (SaaS persist) and local (ingest writes to configurable S3/GCS path or internal DB). Private will default to local with same TTL mechanics.

sam: Any API change for callers? we should avoid breaking clients.

anya: No change to generate API. We add optional explain_id in the response metadata. Existing clients ignore it. New debug endpoints will resolve explain_id -> full trace (authz-guarded).

luis: Also consider an on-demand pull debug feature: user requests explain for a recent request id and we re-run policy with trace-level hooks in a sidecar for exact reproduction (safer than storing everything).

ravi: That helps privacy and storage. But re-run needs identical signals; may be tricky. Document caveats.

maia: Rollout plan suggestion:
- stage 1: shadow-mode only (no persistent traces), collect metrics about time to build explains and size
- stage 2: opt-in tenants + sampling + explain_id returns
- stage 3: default enabled for internal tenants + canary external tenants
- stage 4: wider roll with opt-out controls and per-tenant quotas

anya: Sounds good. I'll open RFC + implementation PRs: runtime hook + adapter contract + small ingest service + admin UI to view traces.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary/infra/trace-ingest deployed to staging at 2026-03-22T18:02:11Z :rocket:

sam: :eyes: pls add perf benchmarks for 4 hardware profiles (cpu-proxy, small-gpu, large-gpu, dedicated pool). Also include results when batching enabled.

anya: Will do. I'll include microbench harness and example curl to fetch an explain_id: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood/trace/{explain_id}`

maia: One more ask — add a flag to redact user-provided prompts by default and a tool to rehydrate them for authorized auditors.

anya: Yup — we'll add a rehydrate workflow gated by IAM + audit log.

luis: Thanks — this will make debugging routing surprises way easier. :+1:

anya: I'll post RFC link when PRs are up. Thanks for the quick checks.
